A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GrokFormer research. Their text, equations, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison, including material moved from v1’s main text into v2’s Appendices A–C.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification, graph-classification and synthetic filter-fitting results in Tables III, V and VI, alongside ablations and computational experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification and filter-fitting results and reports additional order-adaptivity and computational measurements, including Appendix B and Table 8.

M1.justification: The Fourier-parameterized multi-order filters, learned order coefficients, spectral convolution, efficient self-attention, residual encoder and cross-entropy objective are retained. Renaming filter bases and ablation variants, and explicitly writing EMHA in the architecture equation, clarify procedures already described in v1.

E1.justification: The ten real-world node-classification datasets and five graph-classification datasets are unchanged. V2 adds Low-comb as a sixth synthetic filtering target in Section 5.3.1 and Table 4, extending the required frequency patterns within the existing regression task.

E2.justification: V2 adds PolyFormer(Cheb) to graph classification in Table 3 and removes PolyAttn(Cheb) from synthetic filter fitting in Table 4. The computational comparison also narrows to PolyFormer and Specformer. The node-classification comparator set remains unchanged; GPR-GNN/GPRGNN is a naming change.

E3.justification: V2 narrows the node weight-decay search and reports official Penn94 splits in Appendix A.2.2. It replaces Photo timing at hidden dimension 32 with Cora/Penn94 time-and-memory measurements at dimension 64 over 1,000 epochs. Synthetic fitting is described using author-recommended baseline settings rather than v1’s uniform training and matched-parameter controls. These are reported protocol revisions, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The order analysis now examines which learned coefficient dominates alongside maximum order and accuracy, covering all ten node datasets rather than six sensitivity curves. A Citeseer filter visualization and revised computational analysis are added. Conversely, component ablations shrink from fifteen datasets in v1 Table VII to four in v2 Table 5, removing evidence on complex heterophilic graphs such as Chameleon and Squirrel; those ablations are not restored in the appendices.

E5.justification: V1 states that all node datasets use ten random splits. V2 Appendix A.2.2 specifies five runs on official Penn94 splits, although Section 5.1 still says ten random splits. This changes reported run-count information and introduces an inconsistency; it does not establish an actual reduction in runs. Existing dispersion reporting and graph cross-validation are otherwise retained.

E6.justification: Shared main classification scores remain unchanged. V2 adds PolyFormer graph scores, Low-comb results, dominant-order observations and time/memory measurements, while removing most ablation entries and the Photo cost results. Some synthetic SSEs change: the proposed filter’s Low-pass value changes from 0.0016 to 0.0011, and Specformer’s Comb value from 0.0063 to 0.0083. Revised protocol descriptions prevent treating these as controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: V2 introduces Propositions 4.1–4.4 and Appendix C proofs concerning dual adaptability, polynomial-filter and Specformer special cases, universal approximation and permutation equivariance; v1 has no corresponding propositions or proofs. The truncated forward-complexity expression also changes from O(Nd² + KNM + q²d) to O(Nd² + KqM + Nqd).

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a Fourier-based, order- and spectrum-adaptive graph Transformer with strong classification performance. V2 adds an explicit claim to be the first GT with both adaptations and elevates theoretical comparative expressiveness into the abstract and contribution list. These strengthen the stated contribution without replacing the central research objective.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting dominant learned order coefficients to simple versus complex filter requirements and explicitly notes that real-world filter ground truths are unknown. It removes v1’s limitation concerning scarce labels and its unsupervised/transfer-learning directions, instead proposing future filtering without spectral decomposition.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds layer, attention-head and hidden-dimension search ranges, node early-stopping patience, and further graph-training settings. These are newly documented details rather than demonstrated architectural changes. V2 omits v1’s explicit synthetic sample count of 50 images and several training-control details. Hardware, libraries and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds direct citations to KAN and FourierKAN-GCF, together with approximation-theory and Fourier-analysis references, and removes several background references. Positioning remains within the same spectral-GNN and graph-Transformer literature, but Table 1 sharpens the order-versus-spectrum distinction and the new theory asserts special-case relationships to competing filters.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and substantial methodological and experimental explanations are rewritten. V2 reorganizes the narrative around order/spectrum adaptability and theoretical analysis, consolidates experimental details into Appendix A, and places additional analyses and proofs in Appendices B and C. This is extensive restructuring beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the motivating Figure 1, adds an adaptability-comparison table, redesigns order analyses as three-dimensional plots, transposes and contracts the ablation table, and replaces the Photo bubble chart with a time/memory table. Dataset tables and many filter plots move into appendices, alongside substantial document-template and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added Low-comb and order-weight analyses, fuller implementation settings and revised complexity bound are useful. However, ablation coverage and synthetic-control documentation decrease, and Penn94 split descriptions conflict. The new Specformer-subsumption claim is also not established by Appendix C: its proof restricts attention to the identity matrix and assumes an unjustified linear-function/shifted-sine equality in Equation 19. These competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
